newsitem.title: USA: Clinton exhorts firms to hire people off welfare.
newsitem.headline: Clinton exhorts firms to hire people off welfare.

text.p: In what has become a monthly exercise, President Bill Clinton preached his welfare-to-work sermon on Tuesday to executives from 105 companies that have agreed to hire people off public assistance.
Since signing a landmark law ending the 60-year federal entitlement last August, Clinton has repeatedly used the bully pulpit of the White House to exhort businesses to employ welfare recipients.

He did so again on Tuesday at a ceremony in the executive mansion's East Room, gathering executives, Cabinet officials and the governors of Wisconsin and Delaware, Republican Tommy Thompson and Democrat Tom Carper, to highlight his effort.
"The import of the welfare reform law was to change, challenge and end the culture of poverty," Clinton told the executives. "We do not have to have a country with a permanent culture of dependence."

The White House announced that the 105 companies, which include UAL Corp, the parent of United Airlines, and United Parcel Service, have agreed to join a "Welfare to Work Partnership" to promote the idea.

The non-profit group will seek to help companies hire welfare recipients by giving them information, techincal assistance and support and pledged to enlist 1,000 firms in the effort within six months.

Clinton, a Democrat, also urged the Republican-controlled Congress to pass his proposal for $600 million in spending to help welfare recipients find transportation to jobs that may be far from their homes.

Clinton has highlighted the issue every month this year, mentioning it in his inaugural address in January as well as in February's State of the Union speech, devoting a radio address to it in March and announcing in April the federal government itself will hire 10,000 people off welfare by 2000.

The White House estimates that to comply with the welfare law -- which limits aid to five years over a person's lifetime and requires recipients to work after two -- one million people will have to go from welfare to work over the next four years.
